subject: Renewal: usage health review + recommended capacity path
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Romero <alicia@vertexlabs.ai>, Devon Park <devon.park@vertexlabs.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: usage health review + recommended capacity path

Hi Alicia / Devon —

Quick note ahead of our renewal window: I pulled a short usage health snapshot for Vertex Labs (attached) and wanted to flag the key trends and a recommended capacity path so procurement has a starting point. TL;DR: usage is up, latency stable, and we have levers to reduce unit cost without sacrificing latency.

Key signals (Q3 → rolling 30d):
- Average monthly token consumption: 1.9B → 2.1B (30d spike to 2.4B driven by increased embedding calls from Search microservice)
- p95 generation latency: 420ms (no material regressions)
- Error rate: <0.2% for production routes
- Cost per 1k tokens: observed uplift due to heavy long-context generation; potential to reduce by ~18% by switching model mix + enabling prefix caching

Recommended path (what we suggest for the renewal):
1) Move to a 12-month committed tier sized at 2.5B tokens/month with a 3-month ramp schedule. This covers current baseline + expected growth and gives you stable per-token economics.
2) Pilot Dedicated pool for the heavy embedding pipeline (2 GPUs, dedicated for 60 days) — should drop embedding unit cost ~20–30% and remove region-induced variability.
3) Enable prefix/KV caching and try our 4-bit quantized variant on a subset of dev traffic (we can A/B with no impact to accuracy for short prompts).

Attachments: Vertex_Q3_usage_report.pdf (includes daily burn, route breakdown), perf_benchmarks_4bit_vs_fp16.csv (summary bench).

Can we schedule 30 minutes this week to walk procurement through the proposed amendment (term + commit + burst credits)? Available: Tue 10/2 10–12, Wed 10/3 14–16 PT.

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Renewals
Redwood Inference
From: Alicia Romero <alicia@vertexlabs.ai>

Cc: Devon Park <devon.park@vertexlabs.ai>
Date: 2028-10-01T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: usage health review + recommended capacity path

Hannah —

Thanks for the snapshot and clear recommendations. A few clarifying questions before we bring procurement in:
1) Token mix: how much of that 2.4B spike is long-context generation vs embeddings? We care because embeddings are cheaper to optimize with Dedicated.
2) If we agree to the 2.5B commit, can you show a side-by-side of current blended rate vs proposed committed rate (including the 60-day Dedicated pilot economics)?
3) Our SRE team wants to confirm p95 under the Dedicated pilot at scale — can Olga share a short perf expectation doc?

Procurement (procure@vertexlabs.ai) will need line-item pricing and a sample amendment. We are targeted to close the renewal by 10/18 to align with our budget cycle.

Best,
Alicia Romero
Head of Product, Search
Vertex Labs

Alicia —

Short technical follow-up and performance expectations. Attaching a CSV with microbenchmarks (perf_benchmarks_4bit_vs_fp16.csv). Key notes:
- Token breakout from the last 30 days: embeddings ~58%, short-form generation (<=512 tokens) ~30%, long-context generation (~2k tokens) ~12%. The recent spike is primarily embeddings (Search reindex job and increased candidate scoring).
- Dedicated pool recommendation: 2x A100-equivalent GPUs dedicated to embeddings for the pilot. Expected raw cost reduction for embedding calls: 18–28% excluding caching.
- Caching + quantization combined: we estimate up to 35% total unit cost reduction for the embedding-heavy routes with no measurable P95 degradation in our bench runs. p95 on Dedicated + 4-bit quantized model: ~380ms (vs 420ms currently).
- Risk notes: for models with long-context, 4-bit quantization showed minor token-level fidelity differences on pathological examples — we recommend A/B on non-critical production traffic first.

Next steps I can own:
- Run a 7-day A/B test configuration in staging to validate p95 and accuracy delta (need a small sample of your prompts).
- Share the Dedicated pilot runbook (expected timing, rollback, observability hooks).

Attachments: perf_benchmarks_4bit_vs_fp16.csv

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Alicia / Procurement team —

Appreciate the quick back-and-forth. Based on Hannah's snapshot and Olga's bench, here's a clean commercial proposal to get procurement moving:

Proposal (summary)
- Term: 12 months (auto-renew option)
- Commit: 2.5B tokens/month (monthly billing) with a 3-month linear ramp from contract start (month 1 at 1.9B baseline, month 3 at full 2.5B).
- Pricing: 15% discount on list for the committed tier vs current pay-as-you-go blended rate.
- Pilot: 60-day Dedicated embedding pool trial (2x A100-equivalent); pilot costs covered via a phased credit program (we'll provide burst credits to offset setup + test traffic).
- SLA & observability: 99.9% uptime SLA for Dedicated pilot with access to per-route dashboards and token-level cost deltas.

Procurement items enclosed: sample amendment (line-item pricing), SOW for pilot, and a DocuSign envelope to review and sign. Links below:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-78934
- DocuSign: https://docusign.com/DocuSign/envelope/0a1b2c3d4e

If that looks actionable, I'll open the amendment and route to your procure@ address. Target: get signatures by 2028-10-18 to meet your budget timeline.

Ben Carter

Redwood Inference
